examples.ko: 그는 필사적인 노력 끝에 시험에 붙었어요.
examples.en: After desperate effort, he passed the exam.
The child frantically looked for his mother.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 필사적인 표정으로 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: He looked at me with a desperate expression.
We ran desperately to catch the last train.

examples.ko: 필사적으로 달려도 시간에 못 맞출 것 같아요.
examples.en: Even if I run as hard as I can, I don't think I'll make it in time.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 필사적인 수비로 팀을 구했어요.
examples.en: That player saved the team with desperate defense.

explain: '열심히'보다 훨씬 절박해서, 큰 것이 걸려 있는 느낌이에요. 보통 '필사적으로', '필사적인 노력'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is far more urgent than '열심히' (diligently) and feels like something big is at stake. It is usually used as '필사적으로' or '필사적인 노력'.

examples.ko: 필순을 알면 글씨를 예쁘게 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you know the stroke order, you can write neatly.
The stroke order of this Chinese character is a bit hard.

examples.ko: 선생님이 칠판에 필순을 천천히 보여 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher slowly showed us the stroke order on the board.

examples.ko: 필순대로 쓰면 글자 모양이 더 균형 있어요.
examples.en: If you write in stroke order, the letter shape is more balanced.
I got the stroke order wrong, so the character looks strange.

examples.ko: 아이들이 필순을 따라 쓰며 한자를 배워요.
examples.en: The children learn Chinese characters by tracing the stroke order.

explain: 한글이나 한자를 쓸 때 어느 획부터 쓰는지를 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '획순'이라고도 해요. 보통 위에서 아래로, 왼쪽에서 오른쪽으로 쓰는 것이 기본이에요.
explain_en: It refers to which stroke you write first when writing Hangul or Chinese characters. '획순' means the same thing. The basic rule is generally top to bottom and left to right.

examples.ko: 저는 하루 필요량보다 물을 적게 마시고 있어요.
examples.en: I am drinking less water than the amount I need per day.

examples.ko: 아이에게 필요한 영양소의 필요량은 나이마다 달라요.
examples.en: The amount of nutrients a child needs differs by age.
I buy only what I need, so I don't throw food away.
I calculated the amount needed and ordered the ingredients.

examples.ko: 비타민 하루 필요량은 음식으로도 채울 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can also meet the daily vitamin requirement through food.

examples.ko: 운동을 많이 하면 단백질 필요량이 늘어요.
examples.en: If you exercise a lot, your protein requirement increases.

explain: 영양, 물, 전기, 재료처럼 숫자로 잴 수 있는 것에 '이만큼 필요하다'고 말할 때 써요. '하루 필요량'처럼 앞에 기간을 붙이는 경우가 많아요. 짝말은 '충분하다/부족하다'예요.
explain_en: Use it for measurable things such as nutrients, water, electricity or materials when saying how much is needed. A period often comes before it, as in '하루 필요량' (daily requirement). It pairs with '충분하다' (enough) and '부족하다' (short).

en: time of need; being when necessary; being in case of necessity

examples.en: If needed, please contact me anytime.

examples.ko: 필요시에는 회의를 다시 열 수 있어요.
examples.en: If necessary, we can hold the meeting again.

examples.ko: 이 약은 필요시 먹는 약이니까 아플 때만 드세요.
examples.en: This medicine is for when needed, so take it only when you are in pain.

examples.ko: 비상구는 필요시 바로 열 수 있어야 해요.
examples.en: An emergency exit must be openable right away when needed.
Refunds are possible if needed, so don't worry.

examples.ko: 필요시에 쓰려고 우산을 가방에 넣어 뒀어요.
examples.en: I put an umbrella in my bag to use if needed.

explain: '필요할 때'를 줄인 말로, 안내문이나 공지, 메일처럼 글에서 많이 보여요. 대화에서는 보통 '필요하면', '필요할 때'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is a short form of '필요할 때' (when needed) and shows up in notices, announcements and emails. In conversation people usually say '필요하면' or '필요할 때'.

examples.en: Health is a necessary condition for happiness, but not a sufficient one.
Experience is a necessary condition for this job.

examples.ko: 영어 점수는 지원의 필요조건 중 하나예요.
examples.en: An English score is one of the necessary conditions for applying.

examples.ko: 필요조건을 모두 채워도 합격이 보장되지는 않아요.
examples.en: Even if you meet all the necessary conditions, passing is not guaranteed.

examples.ko: 수학 시간에 필요조건과 충분조건의 차이를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In math class I learned the difference between necessary and sufficient conditions.
This certificate is not a necessary condition for getting a job.

explain: '이것이 없으면 안 되는 조건'이에요. 짝말인 '충분조건'(이것만 있으면 되는 조건)과 함께 배우는 경우가 많아요. 일상에서는 '꼭 필요한 조건'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It means a condition you cannot do without. It is often learned together with its counterpart '충분조건' (sufficient condition). In daily talk people also say '꼭 필요한 조건'.

en: second volume; volume two; third volume; last volume

examples.ko: 소설 상권은 읽었는데 하권은 아직 못 샀어요.
examples.en: I read the first volume of the novel, but I haven't bought the last one yet.
The later part of the story is in the last volume.
I went to the library to borrow the last volume.

examples.ko: 이 책은 상권보다 하권이 더 재미있어요.
examples.en: In this book, the last volume is more fun than the first.
Is there a bookstore that sells only the last volume?

examples.ko: 하권 마지막 장에서 저도 모르게 울었어요.
examples.en: I cried without realizing it on the last chapter of the last volume.

explain: 책이 두 권이나 세 권으로 나뉠 때 맨 끝 권을 말해요. 짝말은 '상권'이고, 세 권이면 가운데는 '중권'이라고 해요. 일상에서는 '2권', '마지막 권'처럼 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the last book when a work is split into two or three volumes. Its counterpart is '상권', and the middle of three is '중권'. In daily talk people also say '2권' or '마지막 권'.

en: in fact; in truth; indeed; actually

examples.en: Come to think of it, that's true too.
Well, I thought so at first too.

examples.ko: 하기는 요즘 물가가 너무 올라서 이해가 가요.
examples.en: Then again, prices have gone up so much that I understand.

examples.ko: 하기는 비가 이렇게 오는데 누가 나가고 싶겠어요?
examples.en: Well, with rain like this, who would want to go out?

examples.ko: 하기는 제가 그 사람이라도 화가 났겠어요.
examples.en: Then again, I would have been angry too if I were him.

examples.ko: 하기는 그 식당은 값에 비해 양이 적어요.
examples.en: Well, that restaurant does give small portions for the price.

explain: 상대나 앞의 말을 '그러고 보니 맞네'라고 인정할 때 써요. 대화에서는 '하긴'으로 줄여 말하는 경우가 많아요. '편하기는 하지만'처럼 '-기는 하다' 구조에 들어간 '하기는'과는 달라요.
explain_en: Use it to concede that what was said is right when you think about it. In conversation it is often shortened to '하긴'. It is different from the '-기는 하다' pattern, as in '편하기는 하지만'.

examples.en: I was surprised that the students' answers were all the same.
Everyone's reaction was uniformly good.

examples.ko: 이 거리의 가게 간판이 하나같이 낡았어요.
examples.en: The signs of the shops on this street are all old.
The two people think exactly alike.
The children all raised their hands without exception.
The reviews are all praise, so it's hard to believe.

explain: 대부분 '하나같이'로 써요. '모두'와 달리 하나도 빠짐없이 똑같다는 놀라움이나 평가가 들어 있어요. '하나같다'는 같은 모양이나 같은 마음일 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used as '하나같이'. Unlike '모두' (all), it carries surprise or judgment that everything is the same without exception. '하나같다' is also used when things look alike or people feel alike.

examples.en: You could at least have said goodbye before leaving.

examples.ko: 하다못해 물 한 잔이라도 드시고 가세요.
examples.en: Please have at least a glass of water before you go.

examples.ko: 돈이 없으면 하다못해 라면이라도 같이 먹어요.
examples.en: If you have no money, let's at least eat ramen together.
You should have at least sent one text message.
That store didn't have even tissues.
Please at least buy an umbrella at a convenience store.

explain: '더 큰 건 못 해도 이 정도는'이라는 아쉬움이나 불만이 들어 있어요. 뒤에 '-라도/-이라도'가 자주 와요. 단순히 '적어도'라고 말할 때보다 감정이 더 강해요.
explain_en: It carries a feeling of regret or complaint, meaning even if you can't do more, at least this much. It is often followed by '-라도/-이라도'. It is more emotional than a plain '적어도'.

examples.ko: 그는 십 년을 하루같이 가게 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: He opened his shop every single day for ten years, without change.

examples.ko: 어머니는 하루같이 새벽에 일어나서 밥을 하셨어요.
examples.en: My mother got up at dawn every day without fail to cook.
Thanks to practicing steadily every day, my skills improved.

examples.ko: 선생님은 한 해 동안 하루같이 우리를 챙겨 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher looked after us constantly throughout the year.

examples.ko: 하루같이 같은 길로 출근하니까 좀 지루해요.
examples.en: I go to work by the same road every day, so it's a bit boring.

examples.ko: 그 할아버지는 하루같이 공원에서 운동을 하세요.
examples.en: That grandfather exercises in the park every day without fail.

explain: 오랫동안 변함없이 꾸준하다는 뜻으로 써요. '십 년을 하루같이'처럼 긴 기간 뒤에 자주 붙고, 대체로 성실함을 칭찬하는 느낌이에요. '매일'보다 한결같은 태도가 중심이에요.
explain_en: It means steadily and without change over a long time. It often follows a long period, as in '십 년을 하루같이', and usually praises someone's diligence. Compared with '매일' (every day), the focus is on a consistent attitude.

examples.en: They say mayflies live only a day.

examples.ko: 여름 저녁이면 가로등 주변에 하루살이가 많아요.
examples.en: On summer evenings there are many mayflies around the streetlights.

examples.ko: 연못 위에 하루살이 수백 마리가 날고 있었어요.
examples.en: Hundreds of mayflies were flying over the pond.
I opened the window and a mayfly flew in.
Because of the swarm of mayflies, it's hard to take a walk.
The child saw a mayfly for the first time and found it fascinating.

explain: 벌레 이름이지만 '하루살이처럼 산다'고 하면 미래 계획 없이 그날그날 겨우 산다는 비유로도 써요. 이때는 조금 안타깝거나 부정적인 느낌이에요.

phrases.example: 월급 받으면 다 쓰는 하루살이 인생이 이제 지겨워요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내일 계획 없이 그날그날 겨우 사는 삶을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a life of just getting by day to day with no plan for tomorrow.

explain_en: It is the name of an insect, but '하루살이처럼 산다' is also a figure of speech for living day to day with no plan for the future. That use has a slightly sad or negative tone.

en: as soon as possible; immediately; quickly

examples.en: I hope you recover your health as soon as possible.
Please solve this problem as soon as possible.
I would be grateful if you could reply as soon as possible.
I hope the rain stops as soon as possible.
I have to find a house to move into as soon as possible.
To get better quickly, get plenty of rest.

explain: '빨리'보다 간절한 바람이나 부탁의 느낌이 강하고, 글이나 공손한 말에 잘 어울려요. 같은 뜻으로 '하루빨리'도 써요.
explain_en: It feels more earnest than '빨리', expressing a strong wish or request, and suits writing or polite speech. '하루빨리' is used with the same meaning.

examples.en: I'll give you just one day's worth of this medicine first.
I finished a whole day's work today.
I packed only one day's worth of clothes in my travel bag.
One day's worth of food doesn't seem like enough.

examples.ko: 하루치 월급이 이렇게 적다니 믿기지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't believe a day's pay is this small.
I buy milk in one-day portions.

explain: 하루 동안 쓰거나 해야 하는 양을 말해요. '이틀치', '일주일치'처럼 숫자를 바꿔 쓸 수 있고, 약, 식량, 일, 월급 같은 말과 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: It means the amount you use or must do in one day. You can swap in other periods, as in '이틀치' or '일주일치', and it goes well with medicine, food, work and pay.

examples.en: That new hire challenged the boss like a reckless pup.

examples.ko: 하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다더니 딱 그 모습이에요.
examples.en: As the saying goes, a pup doesn't fear the tiger, and that's exactly him.

examples.ko: 저는 아직 하룻강아지라서 모르는 게 많아요.
examples.en: I'm still a greenhorn, so there's a lot I don't know.

examples.ko: 하룻강아지 같은 소리 하지 말고 경험자의 말을 들어요.
examples.en: Stop talking like a greenhorn and listen to someone experienced.

examples.ko: 하룻강아지가 겁도 없이 큰 개에게 다가갔어요.
examples.en: The little puppy approached the big dog without any fear.
Don't act like a reckless pup in front of your older brother.

explain: 원래는 태어난 지 얼마 안 된 어린 강아지인데, 보통 겁 없이 덤비는 경험 없는 사람을 낮춰서 말해요. 놀리는 말투라서 윗사람에게 쓰면 안 돼요. 자기 자신을 낮출 때는 겸손하게 쓸 수도 있어요.

phrases.example: 하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다더니, 신입이 사장님께 따졌어요.
phrases.en: A newborn puppy doesn't know to fear the tiger.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경험이 없어서 무서운 줄 모르고 겁 없이 덤비는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an inexperienced person who rashly takes on someone far stronger.
phrases.en_equiv: fools rush in where angels fear to tread

explain_en: Literally a very young puppy, it is usually used to put down an inexperienced person who recklessly takes on others. The tone is teasing, so don't use it about someone above you. You can also use it humbly about yourself.

examples.ko: 이 건물 하반부에는 상점이 모여 있어요.
examples.en: Shops are clustered in the lower part of this building.
The lower half of the picture got wet and smeared.
Enlarge the photo of the lower half and look closely.

examples.ko: 몸의 하반부가 차가우면 양말을 신어 보세요.
examples.en: If the lower half of your body feels cold, try wearing socks.

examples.ko: 산의 하반부는 안개에 가려 보이지 않았어요.
examples.en: The lower half of the mountain was hidden by fog.
There is a place to sign in the lower part of the document.

explain: 어떤 물건이나 몸, 그림의 아래쪽 절반을 말해요. 짝말은 '상반부'예요. 올해의 뒤쪽 절반처럼 시간을 말할 때는 '하반기'를 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the lower half of an object, body or picture. Its counterpart is '상반부'. For the second half of a year or other time spans, use '하반기' instead.

examples.en: I board near the university.

examples.ko: 처음 서울에 왔을 때 학교 앞에서 하숙했어요.
examples.en: When I first came to Seoul, I lodged near the school.

examples.ko: 하숙하면 밥을 해 먹지 않아도 돼서 편해요.
examples.en: If you board, you don't have to cook, so it's convenient.
Where do you want to board?
While I boarded, the landlady was good to me.
I plan to board for a short while only during vacation.

explain: 방을 빌리면서 식사도 함께 받는 것을 말해요. 식사 없이 혼자 밥을 해 먹으며 사는 '자취하다'와 달라요. 사는 집은 '하숙집', 사람은 '하숙생'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It means renting a room and getting meals along with it. This differs from '자취하다', where you live alone and cook for yourself. The house is a '하숙집' and the person is a '하숙생'.

examples.en: There are still tickets left for the down-line train.

examples.ko: 사고 때문에 하행선이 막혀서 도착이 늦어졌어요.
examples.en: The down line was blocked by an accident, so my arrival was delayed.
I'm taking the line going down from Seoul to Busan.

examples.ko: 주말 저녁에는 하행선보다 상행선이 더 막혀요.
examples.en: On weekend evenings the up line is more jammed than the down line.
The platform for the down line is on the second basement level.

examples.ko: 고장 때문에 하행선 열차가 잠시 멈췄어요.
examples.en: Because of a breakdown, the down-line train stopped for a while.

explain: 기차나 고속도로에서 서울에서 먼 지방 쪽으로 내려가는 노선을 말해요. 반대로 서울로 올라오는 쪽은 '상행선'이에요. 이동 방향을 말할 때 '내려간다/올라간다'고 하는 한국어 습관과 이어져요.
explain_en: On trains and highways it is the route heading away from Seoul toward the provinces. The opposite, toward Seoul, is '상행선'. It matches the Korean habit of saying you go 'down' to the provinces and 'up' to Seoul.

examples.en: I went to the school during parent consultation week.
The parents gathered on the field and cheered for the children.
The teacher called the student's parent.
I gave the greeting as the parents' representative.

examples.ko: 학부형 중에는 학교 일을 도와주시는 분도 많아요.
examples.en: Among the parents, many help out with school events.

examples.ko: 오늘 학부형 모임이 오후 세 시에 있어요.
examples.en: The parents' meeting is today at three in the afternoon.

explain: 학교에 다니는 학생의 부모를 가리켜요. 같은 뜻으로 '학부모'도 쓰는데, '학부형'은 조금 예스럽게 들릴 수 있어요. 학생 본인에게는 쓰지 않고, 학교나 선생님 입장에서 부모를 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the parents of a student. '학부모' has the same meaning, but '학부형' can sound a little old-fashioned. It is not used for the student, and is used from the school's or teacher's viewpoint when talking about parents.

examples.en: This text is academic in content, so it's difficult.
It was evaluated as academically meaningful research.
They found material of high scholarly value.
A paper has to be written in an academic style.
It hasn't been proven academically.

examples.ko: 교수님은 학술적 용어를 쉽게 풀어 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The professor explained the academic terms in an easy way.

explain: '전문적'은 어느 분야에나 쓰지만 '학술적'은 연구와 논문 쪽에 쓰는 점이 달라요. '학술적 가치', '학술적인 글'처럼 명사 앞에 붙이거나 '학술적으로'로 써요.
explain_en: '전문적' (professional) fits any field, but '학술적' is tied to research and papers. Put it directly before a noun, as in '학술적 가치' or '학술적인 글', or use '학술적으로'.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 서울에서 국제 학술회의가 열려요.
examples.en: An international academic conference will be held in Seoul next month.
I presented my research results at the conference.
Registration for the conference is until this week.
Many foreign scholars also come to the conference.

examples.ko: 저는 학술회의 때문에 부산으로 출장을 가요.
examples.en: I'm going on a business trip to Busan for a conference.

examples.ko: 학술회의 발표 자료를 아직 다 못 만들었어요.
examples.en: I haven't finished making my conference presentation materials yet.

explain: 연구자들이 모여 연구 결과를 발표하고 토론하는 모임이에요. 비슷한 말로 '학술대회', '학회'가 있어요. 영어 단어를 그대로 써서 '컨퍼런스', '세미나'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is a gathering where researchers present and discuss results. Similar words are '학술대회' and '학회'. People also borrow English and say '컨퍼런스' or '세미나'.

en: one step; a single step; one stride

examples.en: When I heard the news of passing, I ran over right away.
You only need to go one more step to reach the goal.

examples.ko: 한걸음 물러서서 상황을 보면 답이 보여요.
examples.en: If you step back and look at the situation, the answer shows up.
The baby took one step and then fell right down.
If you climb slowly, one step at a time, it isn't hard.
I stepped back one step in front of the door.

explain: 발을 한 번 떼어 옮기는 거리나 동작이에요. '한걸음에 달려가다'처럼 쓰면 '곧바로 서둘러'라는 뜻이고, '한걸음 물러서다'는 한발 떨어져서 본다는 뜻으로도 써요. 보통은 '한 걸음'으로 띄어 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: to run over in one stride
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번도 쉬지 않고 곧바로 급히 간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to go right away in a hurry without stopping.

explain_en: It is the distance or motion of moving one foot forward once. '한걸음에 달려가다' means to rush over right away, and '한걸음 물러서다' can also mean stepping back to look at things calmly. It is also often written with a space as '한 걸음'.

examples.en: On my day off, I read books for half the day.
Preparing for the move took half a day.

examples.ko: 한나절이면 이 일을 끝낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can finish this job in half a day.
There was no contact for half a day, so I was worried.

examples.ko: 한나절쯤 걸으면 산 정상에 닿을 거예요.
examples.en: If you walk for about half a day, you will reach the summit.

examples.ko: 아무 소득 없는 회의로 한나절을 그냥 보냈어요.
examples.en: I wasted half a day on a pointless meeting.

explain: 하루의 절반쯤 되는 시간으로, 주로 낮 동안을 말해요. '반나절'과 비슷한 뜻으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 시간이 꽤 걸렸다는 느낌을 줄 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is about half of a day, mainly during daytime hours. It is often used much like '반나절'. It fits well when you want to say something took quite a while.

examples.en: The whole nation cheered for the players with one heart.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 한마음이 되어 위기를 넘겼어요.
examples.en: Our team became of one mind and got through the crisis.

examples.ko: 한마음으로 노력하면 못 할 일이 없어요.
examples.en: If we work with one mind, there is nothing we can't do.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 한마음이라 말하지 않아도 잘 통해요.
examples.en: The two are of one mind, so they understand each other without words.

examples.ko: 반 친구들이 한마음으로 선생님께 선물을 준비했어요.
examples.en: The classmates prepared a gift for the teacher with one mind.

examples.ko: 한마음 한뜻으로 이 일을 꼭 해내요.
examples.en: With one heart and one will, let's get this done.

explain: 여러 사람이 같은 마음으로 뭉친다는 좋은 느낌이 있어요. '한마음으로', '한마음이 되다'처럼 자주 써요. 응원, 협력, 위기 극복 같은 상황에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It has a warm feel of many people uniting with the same heart. It is often used as '한마음으로' or '한마음이 되다'. It suits cheering, cooperation and overcoming a crisis.

en: in one breath; in a single gulp; at a stroke; in one fell swoop

examples.ko: 목이 말라서 물을 한숨에 다 마셨어요.
examples.en: I was thirsty, so I drank all the water in one go.
The novel was so fun that I read it in one sitting.
I climbed the stairs without stopping and now I'm out of breath.
I ran here without stopping, but I was still late.

examples.ko: 배가 고파서 빵을 한숨에 먹어 치웠어요.
examples.en: I was hungry, so I wolfed down the bread in one go.

examples.ko: 이 일을 한숨에 끝내려고 하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't try to finish this job all in one go.

explain: 중간에 쉬지 않고 한 번에 쭉 한다는 뜻이에요. '단숨에'와 거의 같게 쓸 수 있어요. 한숨(sigh)과 모양이 같아서 헷갈릴 수 있지만, '한숨을 쉬다'와는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It means doing something all at once without stopping in between. You can use it almost the same way as '단숨에'. It looks like '한숨' (a sigh) and can be confusing, but it is different from '한숨을 쉬다'.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 한약재를 직접 말려서 팔아요.
examples.en: This shop dries medicinal herbs itself and sells them.
The smell of herbal medicine fills the house.
Grandmother boiled chicken soup with medicinal herbs added.

examples.ko: 시장에서 한약재를 사서 차로 끓여 마셨어요.
examples.en: I bought medicinal herbs at the market and boiled them as tea.
How you use them differs for each medicinal herb.
Store medicinal herbs in a place without moisture.

explain: 한약을 만들 때 쓰는 풀뿌리, 열매, 나무껍질 같은 재료를 말해요. 만들어진 약은 '한약'이라고 해서 서로 구분해요. 시장이나 한의원 근처에서 자주 볼 수 있는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to ingredients such as roots, fruits and bark used to make herbal medicine. The finished medicine is called '한약', so the two are distinguished. You often see the word at markets and near Korean medicine clinics.

examples.en: Traditional Korean medicine regards the body's balance as important.
My younger sibling went to university to study traditional Korean medicine.

examples.ko: 한의학 치료를 받고 허리 통증이 많이 좋아졌어요.
examples.en: After traditional Korean medicine treatment, my back pain improved a lot.

examples.ko: 서양 의학과 한의학은 접근 방식이 달라요.
examples.en: Western medicine and traditional Korean medicine take different approaches.

examples.ko: 한의학 박물관에 가 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever been to a traditional Korean medicine museum?
Traditional Korean medicine often uses acupuncture and herbal medicine.

explain: 한국에서 오래 전해 온 의학을 말해요. 일하는 사람은 '한의사', 병원은 '한의원'이라고 해요. 서양식 의학은 보통 '양방'이라고 하고, 한의학 쪽은 '한방'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the medicine passed down in Korea over a long time. The practitioner is a '한의사' and the clinic is a '한의원'. Western-style medicine is usually called '양방', while the Korean side is also called '한방'.

examples.en: I was so tired that I slept for a bit and woke up.
I couldn't sleep a wink on the train.

examples.ko: 한잠 푹 자고 나니 머리가 맑아요.
examples.en: After a deep sleep, my head is clear.
I'll get a nap and then study again.
The baby fell asleep and became quiet.
The rain stopped while I was sleeping.

explain: 깊이 한 번 자는 잠을 말해요. '한잠도 못 자다'처럼 부정과 함께 쓰면 조금도 못 잤다는 강조가 돼요. '한숨 자다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It means one stretch of deep sleep. With a negative, as in '한잠도 못 자다', it stresses that you couldn't sleep at all. People also say '한숨 자다'.

examples.en: A ray of sunlight shone through the clouds.
After a brief shower passed, it became cool.
A single beam of light appeared in the darkness.

examples.ko: 한줄기 바람이 불어와 땀을 식혀 줬어요.
examples.en: A gust of wind came and cooled my sweat.
A single tear rolled down my cheek.

examples.ko: 그는 마지막까지 한줄기 희망을 놓지 않았어요.
examples.en: He did not let go of a thread of hope until the end.

explain: 빛, 비, 바람, 눈물처럼 가늘고 길게 이어지는 것을 셀 때 써요. '한줄기 희망'처럼 작지만 이어지는 마음에도 쓰여요. 보통 '한 줄기'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: Use it to count things that run long and thin, such as light, rain, wind and tears. It also works for feelings that are small but lasting, as in '한줄기 희망'. It is also often written with a space as '한 줄기'.

examples.en: I sweated heavily in the steam room.
The weather today is hot like a sauna.

examples.ko: 찜질방 한증막에는 너무 오래 있지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't stay too long in the sauna room at the jjimjilbang.

examples.ko: 한증막에 들어가면 숨이 막힐 것 같아요.
examples.en: When I go into the steam room, I feel like I can't breathe.
We decided to go to the sauna with family on the weekend.
I ate boiled eggs inside the sauna room.

explain: 찜질방 등에서 아주 뜨겁게 데운 방을 말해요. 날씨가 몹시 더울 때 '한증막 같다'는 비유로도 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로 '사우나'가 있지만 한증막은 한국식 뜨거운 방 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 에어컨이 고장 나서 교실이 한증막 같아요.
phrases.en: to be like a steam room
phrases.nuance_ko: 실내나 날씨가 숨 막힐 만큼 몹시 덥다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for a room or weather that is stiflingly hot.

explain_en: It refers to a very hot room, such as in a jjimjilbang. People also use it as a figure of speech, '한증막 같다', when the weather is extremely hot. '사우나' is a similar word, but 한증막 feels more like a Korean-style hot room.

examples.en: A beach business is a summer-only trade.

examples.ko: 벚꽃은 봄 한철만 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Cherry blossoms can only be seen during the spring season.

examples.ko: 한철 입고 말 옷은 사지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't buy clothes I'll only wear for one season.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 한철 인기를 끌다가 사라졌어요.
examples.en: That singer was popular for a while and then disappeared.
Mosquitoes decrease once the summer season passes.

examples.ko: 한철 바쁜 시기만 지나면 좀 쉴 수 있어요.
examples.en: Once the busy season is over, I can rest a bit.

explain: 어떤 일이 잘되는 한 시기나 한 계절을 말해요. '여름 한철', '한철 장사'처럼 짧게 지나가는 때라는 느낌이 있어요. 오래가지 않고 잠깐이라는 뜻으로 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It refers to one period or season when something thrives. As in '여름 한철' or '한철 장사', it gives a feeling of a short window that passes. It is often used to mean something doesn't last long.

examples.en: I got paid, so I'll treat you today.
I treated my team members to celebrate my promotion.
If you passed, you have to treat us!
My friend got a job and decided to treat us.
The person who treats is the one who pays.

examples.ko: 이번 주말에 제가 점심 한턱낼 테니 오세요.
examples.en: I'll treat you to lunch this weekend, so come over.

explain: 좋은 일이 있을 때 다른 사람들에게 음식이나 술자리 등을 대접하는 말이에요. 말할 때는 '한턱 쏘다'라고도 해요. 그냥 밥값을 나눠 내는 것과 달리 한 사람이 기쁨을 나누며 사는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It means to treat others to a meal or outing when something good happens. In speech people also say '한턱 쏘다'. Unlike splitting the bill, it feels like one person paying to share their happiness.

en: for life; all one's life; throughout life

examples.en: My grandfather farmed all his life.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 한평생 잊지 못할 거예요.
examples.en: I won't forget that person for the rest of my life.

examples.ko: 한평생 한 직장에서 일하기는 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to work at one workplace your whole life.
My mother lived her whole life for her children.
In my whole life, this is the first time something like this has happened.
They donated the money they saved over a lifetime to the school.

explain: '평생'과 거의 같은 뜻이에요. '한평생'이 글이나 어르신의 삶을 이야기할 때 더 자주 쓰여요. 보통 '한평생 ~하며 살다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '평생'. '한평생' appears more often in writing and when talking about an older person's life. It is usually used as '한평생 ~하며 살다'.
